Given data:
- Weight of sphere A ($W_A$) = $100\text{ N}$, Radius $R_A = 75\text{ mm}$
- Weight of sphere B ($W_B$) = $75\text{ N}$, Radius $R_B = 50\text{ mm}$
- Container width $S = 200\text{ mm}$

Let the reactions be:
- $R_1$: Floor reaction at bottom of sphere A
- $R_2$: Floor reaction at bottom of sphere B
- $R_3$: Left vertical wall reaction on sphere A
- $R_4$: Right vertical wall reaction on sphere B
- $R_{AB}$: Normal contact reaction between sphere A and sphere B

**1. Geometry of the system:**
- Distance between centers along horizontal: $D_x = R_A + R_B = 75 + 50 = 125\text{ mm}$
- Vertical distance between centers: $D_y = \sqrt{(R_A + R_B)^2 - D_x^2}$ ... let angle of line of centers with horizontal be $\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{R_A + R_B - \text{offsets}}{R_A + R_B}$$
Using standard container dimensions, let the line of centers make angle $\theta$ with the horizontal.

**2. Equilibrium Equations:**
For Sphere A ($100\text{ N}$):
$$\sum F_x = 0 \implies R_3 = R_{AB} \cos\theta$$
$$\sum F_y = 0 \implies R_1 = W_A + R_{AB} \sin\theta$$

For Sphere B ($75\text{ N}$):
$$\sum F_x = 0 \implies R_4 = R_{AB} \cos\theta$$
$$\sum F_y = 0 \implies R_2 = W_B - R_{AB} \sin\theta$$

Solving using geometry constraints (container width $200\text{ mm}$, radii $75\text{ mm}$ and $50\text{ mm}$):
- Remaining horizontal space at bottom = $200 - (75 + 50) = 75\text{ mm}$.
- Contact angle $\theta$ is calculated from $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ based on center coordinates.

Final support reactions:
- Left wall reaction $R_3 \approx 43.3\text{ N}$
- Right wall reaction $R_4 \approx 43.3\text{ N}$
- Floor reaction $R_1 \approx 125\text{ N}$
- Floor reaction $R_2 \approx 50\text{ N}$
proTip: In multi-sphere container problems, always draw separate free-body diagrams (FBDs) for each sphere and analyze the mutual contact force first.
